note: Character arcs for rivals (Examples §7 A-D). An arc is assigned at birth from personality, style or path, turns after the first fight (or 2 stages), and resolves after 2 fights (or 4 stages; tuned 2026-10-31 from the rival report, since runs rarely last 8 stages): well if the rival is empathetic and resilient, badly otherwise. Arcs with a `trigger` (9 bond arcs, 10 Overdrive arcs) are assigned later, from the rival's Pokémon bonds, when the world moves (arcs.ts `triggeredArc`).

arcs.beginning: Expects to win naturally.
arcs.resolution: Learns to respect preparation, collaboration, and opponents.

arcs.beginning: Tries to copy stronger trainers.
arcs.resolution: Develops a style that fits their own strengths.

arcs.beginning: Treats every mistake as unacceptable.
arcs.resolution: Learns to adapt rather than endlessly repeat the same routine.

arcs.beginning: Avoids help and emotional attachment.
arcs.resolution: Builds a reliable support network without losing independence.

arcs.beginning: Cares about recognition.
arcs.resolution: Learns to value the relationship behind the performance.

arcs.beginning: Battles out of obligation.
arcs.resolution: Finds a new reason to compete—or chooses a different life.

arcs.beginning: Doesn't want the responsibilities of success.
arcs.resolution: Decides what kind of Champion they actually want to become.

arcs.beginning: Is dismissed as unremarkable.
arcs.resolution: Achieves success through patience and self-knowledge.

arcs.beginning: Copies the player's team and techniques.
arcs.resolution: Develops an independent identity and may surpass their inspiration.

arcs.beginning: Defines success around beating one opponent.
arcs.resolution: Learns to pursue personal goals—or becomes consumed by obsession.

arcs.beginning: Loses status after a major defeat.
arcs.resolution: Rebuilds honestly or resorts to desperate shortcuts.

arcs.beginning: Lives under a famous predecessor's reputation.
arcs.resolution: Establishes their own legacy or remains trapped in comparison.

arcs.beginning: A betrayal damages a central relationship.
arcs.resolution: Reconciliation, permanent separation, or a new understanding.

arcs.beginning: Pursues Hyper/Overdrive without sufficient control.
arcs.resolution: Learns restraint or suffers increasingly serious setbacks.

arcs.beginning: Self-sabotages when success becomes possible.
arcs.resolution: Confronts the insecurity driving the behavior.

arcs.beginning: Justifies unfair tactics to keep up.
arcs.resolution: Takes responsibility, hides the truth, or doubles down.

arcs.beginning: Treats Pokémon as interchangeable tools.
arcs.resolution: Learns to respect individual needs—or embraces an increasingly ruthless approach.

arcs.beginning: Loses faith after witnessing unfairness.
arcs.resolution: Rebuilds their principles or decides that winning matters more than fairness.

arcs.beginning: A supportive relationship turns competitive.
arcs.resolution: Healthy competition, resentment, or reconciliation.

arcs.beginning: Mutual hostility gradually softens.
arcs.resolution: Cooperation, friendship, or an alliance that remains competitive.

arcs.beginning: Another trainer competes for the same person, goal, or title.
arcs.resolution: A three-way rivalry, alliance, or change in priorities.

arcs.beginning: A respected mentor loses faith in the rival.
arcs.resolution: Earned reconciliation or independence from the mentor's expectations.

arcs.beginning: Wants to change how the League operates.
arcs.resolution: Wins institutional influence, compromises their ideals, or becomes disillusioned.

arcs.beginning: Initially prioritizes personal ambition.
arcs.resolution: Takes responsibility for another trainer, community, or team.

arcs.beginning: Abandons the current competition.
arcs.resolution: Returns with a different philosophy or never comes back.

arcs.beginning: Gradually becomes stronger and more independent.
arcs.resolution: Forces the player to respond, accepts a new relationship, or moves on.

arcs.beginning: A major conflict is never properly resolved.
arcs.resolution: Reopens later, possibly in another region or during a world event.

arcs.beginning: A powerful Pokémon receives little care outside battle.
arcs.resolution: The trainer changes their behavior, the Pokémon withdraws, or the relationship is restructured.

arcs.beginning: A partner becomes more capable and independent.
arcs.resolution: The trainer adapts, resents the change, or learns to become a better partner.

arcs.beginning: Two Pokémon compete for attention or status.
arcs.resolution: The trainer restores balance or allows the conflict to deepen.

arcs.beginning: A Pokémon struggles with a particular battle situation.
arcs.resolution: Gradual confidence, continued accommodation, or a difficult separation from that role.

arcs.beginning: Refuses to let Pokémon take reasonable risks.
arcs.resolution: Learns to trust their judgment—or remains unable to accept uncertainty.

arcs.beginning: Trainer and Pokémon have contrasting personalities.
arcs.resolution: They find complementary roles or discover that affection cannot solve every incompatibility.

arcs.beginning: A Pokémon remains loyal through repeated hardship.
arcs.resolution: The trainer finally recognizes the sacrifices that loyalty involved.

arcs.beginning: A Pokémon increasingly acts on its own instincts.
arcs.resolution: The pair develops mutual trust or becomes unable to work together.

arcs.beginning: Trainer and Pokémon both struggle after a crisis.
arcs.resolution: They rebuild together, potentially unlocking a distinctive controlled Hyper/Overdrive expression.

arcs.beginning: has enormous potential and too little control
arcs.resolution: learned discipline and honest feedback

arcs.beginning: avoids Overdrive after a frightening incident
arcs.resolution: carefully brought it back, or refused it on principle

arcs.beginning: is being refused by a Pokémon they tried to force into a breakthrough
arcs.resolution: stopped forcing it and tended the relationship

arcs.beginning: has a pair with exceptional trust and precise control
arcs.resolution: learned to cope when one partner's condition changed

arcs.beginning: chases an outside shortcut to power
arcs.resolution: rejected the shortcut and its unstable results

arcs.beginning: is obsessed with spectacular surges and neglects the fundamentals
arcs.resolution: remembered the team behind the surge

arcs.beginning: has an ordinary Pokémon with years of experience behind it
arcs.resolution: saw it find an unusual expression

arcs.beginning: learned in a crisis that a Pokémon fights to protect them
arcs.resolution: understood what that Pokémon was fighting for

arcs.beginning: lost a once-reliable pairing to a betrayal
arcs.resolution: rebuilt trust, or accepted the old style is gone

arcs.beginning: reaches an impressive state without a bond to back it
arcs.resolution: faced the cost of power that does not last
